title: I bought the HIGHEST quality bike frame from a Chinese OEM for $800 (Lightcarbon LCR017D)

takeaways.text: He estimates about £700 delivered depending on import tax; the frameset is ordered by email (no web shop) and arrived three weeks after he ordered at Eurobike.
Every alignment-critical surface (bottom-bracket faces, headset seats, brake mounts, dropouts) is machined rather than masked, and the frame and fork interiors were immaculate under the borescope.
The T47 68 mm shell gives better tool engagement than T47 86.5; checked in a lathe and on his bearing rig, the bottom-bracket alignment was within about 0.02 mm.

Details include a serrated seat clamp, a Di2 battery holder, blanking plugs and a pinned, keyed headset wedge ring that stops the compression ring rotating against the steerer, a common cause of steerer fretting.
Weighed: integrated bar 361 g, seatpost 153 g, headset hardware 150 g and Di2 holder 44 g; the spoken frame and fork weights are garbled in the captions and are not used here.
LightCarbon described tiered QA levels with different jig-check frequency (from none to every fifth frame); he ordered the top tier without a full manual or retail box.
He found it the easiest bike he has assembled because everything aligned; downsides are plain packaging, no manual at his tier and ordering by email.

disclosure: Hambini says he bought the frame himself after meeting LightCarbon at Eurobike and specified its quality-control tier; no sponsorship is stated.
summary: Engineer's inspection, weigh-in and build notes on a LightCarbon LCR017-D ordered at the top quality-control tier.
